A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Relational Visual Similarity and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and supplementary material. All 14 pages of each version support reliable matching and comparison.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 report original retrieval experiments, a human-preference study and analogical image-generation benchmarking, with numerical results in Figures 6 and 8 and Table 2.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports annotation agreement and group-retention outcomes in supplementary Section 9.

M1.justification: The image-filtering, group-based anonymous-captioning and contrastive relsim training procedures remain unchanged. Specifying Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct where v1 used less specific Qwen names clarifies the implementation without establishing a changed model or procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the LAION-2B-derived 114,881-image corpus, 532 curated image groups, relational retrieval and the 200-pair analogical-generation evaluation. Section 9 adds curation information for this retained coverage, without introducing another dataset, domain or task.

E2.justification: The retrieval and user-study comparator sets remain unchanged, as do the tuned CLIP/DINO comparisons in Figure 6. Table 2 retains FLUX-Kontext, Bagel, Qwen-Image, GPT4o-Image and Nano-Banana. The newly cited works are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Both retain the reported 100k/14k training/test split, 28k-image retrieval database, 1,000 queries, GPT-4o scoring and 300 triplets per user-study comparator. Training remains 15k iterations with batch size 64 on eight A100 GPUs. Newly disclosed annotation procedures do not establish revisions to these settings.

E4.justification: Section 9 adds limited evidence about annotation consistency: 92% agreement among three image annotators and unanimous group verification with 85% retained. This supplements assessment of data quality; the captioning comparisons, tuned-encoder ablations, similarity-space analysis and qualitative case studies remain unchanged.

E5.justification: v2 first reports inter-annotator agreement for image selection, including the three-annotator count and 92% agreement statistic. This adds annotation-reliability reporting. Benchmark uncertainty reporting, including Table 2's ± values, and run/seed information remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Section 9 newly reports 92% inter-annotator agreement and 85% group retention. These do not replace the retained 93% filtering-model agreement with humans. Benchmark results are unchanged, including relsim's 6.77 in Figure 6, the 42.5–60.7% preference range in Figure 8 and every Table 2 entry.

T1.justification: Sections 3–3.2 retain the same relational-similarity assumption, cosine-similarity formulation, embedding normalization, temperature-scaled scores and InfoNCE objective. No mathematical definitions, derivations or proofs are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about relational visual similarity, the 114k-image dataset, relsim and retrieval/generation applications. The added documentation does not introduce a new central contribution or change the claims' scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning group captions, VLM knowledge and complementary similarity types remain intact. The limitations concerning curated groups, captioning biases/hallucinations and multiple possible relational mappings are unchanged. Rephrasing which similarity is better as when to use each does not substantively alter the argument.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct designation and adds explicit code/data pointers in Section 7. New Section 9 documents annotator qualifications, the 15k-image sampling pool, example-based instructions, group proposal and verification procedures. These are additional disclosures, not evidence that the experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: The introduction adds citations to Rosenfeld et al.'s Totally Looks Like and Shechtman and Irani's Matching Local Self-Similarities Across Images and Videos alongside the discussion of existing similarity models' limitations. The related-work narrative and novelty positioning otherwise remain unchanged; bibliographic corrections do not represent additional works.

P1.justification: v2 adds supplementary Section 9, relocates Data Attributions from the main text to the supplement, updates acknowledgments and terminology, and corrects Section 5's reference from Figure 11 to Figure 10. Most prose and the main section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 loses its faint background grid, several figures are resized or repositioned, and Table 2 moves from the right to the left column. Supplementary page 12 accommodates Section 9 and the relocated attribution. The figure/table inventory and displayed examples are retained; Figures 14–15 are visually identical.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves transparency through annotation procedures and agreement reporting, a more specific model designation, access pointers and a corrected figure reference. The scientific method and benchmark evidence remain unchanged. The gains are limited because Section 9 does not explain how approximately 400 proposed groups and 85% retention relate to the stated total of 532 groups.
